noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

appliesTo.description:
Which kinds of structure this annotation is applicable to. This will one or more of:
 - `type` for a type declaration
 - `field` for any field declaration
 - `function` for a method declaration
 - `valueType` for a (value) type within another declaration

allowsOverride.description:
Whether this annotation can be changed by a mixin type.
If not, types inherit annotations, but cannot change them.

allowsRemixOverride.description:
Whether this annotation can be changed by a remix type.
If not, remix types inherit annotations, but cannot change them.

declarationOnly.description:
Whether this annotation can be only be specified in the original field declaration.
If not, annotations can be added to override fields.

docPills.description:
Map of "pills" added to documentation to flag special features of the type or field. Each key in the map is the
text of a pill and the corresponding value is an expression which is evaluated to determine whether the pill is
shown or not.

The keys (pill text) should be lower case and short. For example, some built-in pills are "required" and
"abstract".

configurable.description:
Whether this Annotation is configurable.

@see TypeAnnotationConfig

value.description:
If specified on an annotation field, this indicates that this field may be used as the "value" field of the
short-form annotation. Only a single field on each annotation may be marked this way.

For example:
```type
type Ann.Puppy mixes Annotation {
  @annotation(value=true)
  cuteness: int
}
```

Then the short annotation may be used: `@puppy(11)` is equivalent to `@puppy(cuteness=11)`.

Note that if the annotation has a field named "_value_", this behavior is enabled and the annotation is not
required.

title:
The `@annotation` annotation marks a type as being an annotation on a piece of metadata.

Here's an example:

```c3typ
@annotation(appliesTo=['field'])
type Ann.Precious {
  howMuch: int
}
```

This creates the `@precious` annotation with an optional field, so these usages are valid:
```type
type Example {
  @precious
  emeralds: int

  @precious(howMuch=9)
  rubies: int
}
```

Annotation types are used extensively by the platform, but can also be defined by applications.
Any type annotated with the @annotation annotation becomes itself an annotation and can be used
by any packages that the depend on the package it is defined in.

Note that annotations have also been called "extensions" since they are ways to extend the metadata
beyond the minimal structure.

Annotation types are kept separate from regular types to avoid confusion, because they are inner types
of the {@link Ann} type. When searching for them in documentation, prefix then with "Ann." to find them.
For example, this annotation is named "Ann.Annotation".

For annotations that typically have only a single field, there is a shortcut, value-only syntax for using that
annotation. This works if the field is named "_value_" or #value is set by annotation.

@see Annotatable
name: Ann.Annotation
